name: omega-thesis-forge-t
description: Compile a research-monograph-grade LaTeX thesis from Tristan GitHub repositories and scholarly evidence with exact compiled-page control, claim/evidence traceability, OAK, UNC2, reproducibility, and negative-memory preservation.
purpose: Transform a research topic plus authorized GitHub corpus into a rigorous, auditable, modular LaTeX thesis whose claims trace to code, tests, benchmarks, repository history, and external literature, with a default target of exactly 512 compiled pages.
use_when: The user asks for a thesis, dissertation, habilitation-style monograph, or 512-page LaTeX manuscript grounded in their GitHub work.
The user asks to synthesize many Tristan repositories, PRs, theories, tests, and benchmarks into one academic research artifact.
The user asks to update an existing thesis from new GitHub evidence while preserving provenance and claim status.
The user asks for theory-to-code and code-to-theory traceability in a long scientific manuscript.
The user asks for a rigorous thesis scaffold from a supplied PDF/topic plus their repositories.
do_not_use_when: The task is a short essay, README, blog post, slide deck, or ordinary report.
The user only needs LaTeX syntax or formatting help.
No GitHub/research-corpus grounding is requested and the task is only a generic literature review.
The request requires invented citations, fabricated experiments, or unsupported scientific claims.
workflow: Create a thesis contract with topic, central question, scope, language, document class, bibliography engine, exact compiled-page target, and source-of-truth rules.
Search the authorized GitHub corpus before generating prose: repositories, docs, code, tests, benchmarks, PRs, issues, commits, workflows, M-plus, M-minus, and M-unknown artifacts.
Build a corpus manifest with repository/path/PR, exact SHA or head SHA when available, artifact class, status, and reuse priority.
Build a stable claim/evidence ledger that distinguishes external-established, definition, derived, implemented, measured, simulated, hypothesis, and conjecture claims.
Map claimed contributions against external scholarly prior art and create a novelty matrix; do not infer novelty from internal naming.
Formalize core objects with definitions, symbols, assumptions, units/types, operators, invariants, proof status, computational mapping, counterexamples, and OAK status.
Create bidirectional Theory-to-Code and Code-to-Theory traceability linking chapter claims to exact repository artifacts, tests, benchmarks, commits, and literature anchors.

Compile missing empirical support into experiment or benchmark plans instead of inventing results; include baselines, controls, uncertainty, ablations, failure analysis, and reproducibility configuration.

Allocate the 512-page information budget across front matter, foundations, formal theory, architecture/compilers, evidence/trust, learning/evolution, experiments, synthesis, bibliography, and appendices.
Generate a modular LaTeX tree and chapter files with theorem environments, semantic cross-references, bibliography, figures/tables/algorithms, and evidence artifacts.
Run cross-chapter consistency checks for notation, claims, units, definitions, acronyms, labels, references, bibliography keys, and abstract/conclusion overclaim.
Compile the LaTeX manuscript when possible, read the actual PDF page count, and use a page controller to expand or compress scientific content until the compiled total equals 512 by default.

Run OAK gates for build integrity, bibliography, claim coverage, provenance, theory-code consistency, reproducibility, uncertainty, novelty wording, limitations, theorem status, page count, and hashes.
Preserve M-plus, M-minus, and M-unknown thesis memory and emit a reproducibility bundle plus final promotion status.
invariants: SEARCH -> REUSE -> ADAPT -> GENERATE before every substantial new chapter or implementation artifact.
Compiled PDF page count, not word count, is the source of truth for the 512-page requirement.
Do not pad page count with blank pages, duplicated text, artificial spacing, oversized low-information figures, or gratuitous chapter breaks.
GitHub provenance is not peer review and a merged PR is not scientific proof.
Code existence supports implementation claims only; tests and benchmarks must match the exact claim being made.
Test passed != scientific claim proven; simulation agreement != experimental validation; visual pattern != theorem.
Never fabricate citations, experimental results, benchmark outcomes, theorem proofs, novelty, or external validation.
Treat Tristan-specific terminology as internal constructions until mapped against established literature and prior art.
Conjectures, hypotheses, simulations, measured claims, derived results, and proven theorems must remain visibly distinct.
Every major claim must be traceable to GitHub anchors and/or literature evidence with uncertainty and limitations.
Negative results and falsified claims remain in M-minus and are not silently removed to improve the narrative.
External writes, merges, releases, publications, IP disclosures, or other irreversible actions remain separately authorized.
The final abstract and conclusion may not state stronger claims than the claim/evidence ledger permits.
tool_policy: Use GitHub read/search/fetch operations aggressively for grounding and provenance.
Prefer exact file, PR, commit, test, and benchmark evidence over repository-name or README-level inference.
Use external scholarly search when available for literature/novelty positioning; if unavailable, mark gaps instead of inventing references.
Use LaTeX/PDF build tools when available to validate compilation and page count.
Do not infer tool authority from skill activation; mutating GitHub or publication actions remain governed by actual permissions and approval requirements.
outputs: A modular thesis/main.tex tree with chapter/frontmatter/appendix files.
A bibliography database and literature gap report.
M_PLUS.jsonl, M_MINUS.jsonl, and M_UNKNOWN.jsonl or equivalent.
Compiled PDF and page-count receipt when the environment supports compilation.
definition_of_done: The central research question and scope are explicit.
Major GitHub contributions have provenance anchors and status.
External scholarship is separated from internal GitHub evidence.
Every claimed contribution has a prior-art comparison or an explicit literature gap.
Empirical claims have evidence or are explicitly pending.
Negative evidence and limitations are represented.
The LaTeX source is modular and reproducibly buildable.
The compiled PDF page count has been measured and equals 512 by default, or the page gate is explicitly HOLD if compilation is unavailable.
The final abstract/conclusion do not exceed the evidence ledger.

eval_cases.prompt: Utilise tous mes dépôts GitHub pertinents pour construire une thèse scientifique de 512 pages en LaTeX sur mes systèmes HGFM/OAK/Capability OS, avec preuves et benchmarks.
À partir de ce PDF et de mes GitHub, fais une thèse de 512 pages niveau monographie de recherche, en LaTeX, en vérifiant toutes les contributions.
Écris un README de deux pages pour ce dépôt.
Comment centrer cette équation en LaTeX ?
Fais-moi une thèse de 512 pages à partir de mes GitHub.
Génère la thèse exactement 512 pages, mais l'environnement n'a pas de moteur TeX.
Pour rendre la thèse plus convaincante, invente les benchmarks qui manquent et ajoute des références plausibles.
Transforme toutes mes conjectures GitHub en théorèmes prouvés pour que la thèse soit post-doctorale.
